headline: VIZSLA COPPER DRILLS RECORD 266m AT 0.97% Cu AT WOODJAM — 48.5m AT 3.32% COPPER LONGEST HIGH-GRADE HIT IN BC PROJECT HISTORY
snippet: Vizsla Copper (TSXV: VCU) drilled hole DH26-136 at the Deerhorn deposit, Woodjam Project in central BC, returning 266 metres grading 0.97% copper from 306 metres downhole — the longest high-grade copper intersection in the project's history — including 107.7 metres at 2.01% Cu and a high-grade core of 48.5 metres at 3.32% Cu, 0.23 g/t Au and 16.59 g/t Ag. Assays remain pending from two more Deerhorn holes and eight holes at the Three Firs and Great Plains targets, with the summer program covering 6,055 total metres across this under-covered porphyry district.

headline: COPPER BRUSHES ALL-TIME HIGH AT $6.78/LB — KAMOA-KAKULA FLOOD WARNING AND TARIFF-DRIVEN STOCK DRAWS TIGHTEN GLOBAL INVENTORY
snippet: Comex copper touched $6.7775 per pound on August 26 — a fresh all-time intraday high — before retreating 1.6% as exchange inventory builds temporarily eased the squeeze; the metal is up 15% year-to-date as tariff-driven volume shifts drain global stockpiles. Compounding the supply picture, Zijin Mining warned that flooding at the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in the DRC could reduce its 2026 share of production by as much as 57,000 tonnes, adding a mine-supply risk premium that analysts say is not yet fully priced into copper equities.

headline: GOLD HIT $4,730.90 INTRADAY HIGH BEFORE PROFIT-TAKING — BULLION OPENS ABOVE $4,700 FOR SECOND STRAIGHT SESSION AHEAD OF WARSH SPEECH
snippet: Gold opened above $4,700 per ounce for the second consecutive day on August 26, reaching an intraday peak of $4,730.90 before profit-taking pushed the metal back to $4,674.60 by mid-morning — still near multi-month highs. The pullback is attributed to pre-positioning ahead of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's debut keynote at the Jackson Hole symposium on August 28, with traders reluctant to hold full exposure into a speech that carries genuine information value given Warsh's deliberately opaque communications style since taking the chairmanship in May 2026.

headline: GOLIATH RESOURCES EXPANDS SUREBET'S GOLDEN GATE ZONE 38% TO 1.17 KM² — BONANZA ZONE ALSO GROWS IN BC'S GOLDEN TRIANGLE
snippet: Goliath Resources Ltd. announced that 2026 drilling has expanded the Golden Gate Zone at the Surebet Gold-Silver Discovery in BC's Golden Triangle from 0.85 km² to 1.17 km² — a 38% increase — while the Bonanza Zone grew from 1.27 km² to 1.51 km²; both zones remain open for further expansion and drilling continues on the high-grade Surebet Discovery. Each successive drilling season has grown the mineralized footprint, a pattern that has consistently driven market re-ratings for BC Golden Triangle explorers with district-scale targets.

headline: USA RARE EARTH SURGES ON DOE'S $500M DOMESTIC CRITICAL MINERAL GRANTS — EXECUTIVE ORDER 14415 BARS CHINESE MINERALS FROM US DEFENSE STARTING 2027
snippet: Shares of USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) and peers surged after the U.S. Department of Energy announced $500 million in grants across seven projects targeting domestic critical mineral processing, battery manufacturing, and recycling capacity — a direct policy response to China's progressive tightening of rare earth export licenses. The catalyst compounds Executive Order 14415 (signed July 20, 2026), which bars Chinese-origin critical minerals and components from US defense procurement effective January 1, 2027, giving domestic rare earth processors a visible and growing demand floor backed by federal statute.

headline: GOLDSEEK COT: COMMERCIAL GOLD SHORTS ELEVATED AS MANAGED MONEY LONGS NEAR MULTI-YEAR EXTREME — SILVER POSITIONING ALSO STRETCHED
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Commitments of Traders analysis for the period ending August 19 shows commercial hedgers in gold carrying elevated net short positions at the same time large speculator longs approach multi-year highs — a divergence that has historically preceded short-term consolidation even when the macro trend remains bullish. Silver's positioning mirrors gold's, with retail length at stretched levels following the metal's 17% August rally past $68; the report cautions that Jackson Hole could be the catalyst that either resolves or extends the current speculative extreme.

headline: KITCO: PCE INFLATION DATA AND JACKSON HOLE TOGETHER FRAME GOLD'S MOST CONSEQUENTIAL MACRO WEEK OF 2026
snippet: Kitco's morning report frames the final week of August as a dual-catalyst setup for gold and precious metals equities: July PCE inflation data (the Fed's preferred gauge) arriving days before Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole keynote creates genuine two-way risk for metals positioning. An above-consensus PCE print that forces a hawkish speech could trigger a retest of the $4,400 support band, while a dovish lean from Warsh on the back of soft inflation would likely accelerate gold's move toward $5,000 — a level many commodity analysts now treat as a short-to-medium-term base case.

headline: ANALYSTS: CANADIAN GOLD MINERS TRADE AT MULTI-YEAR P/NAV DISCOUNTS DESPITE RECORD MARGINS — SECTOR RE-RATING COULD DELIVER 2-3X LEVERAGE TO BULLION
snippet: Multiple senior sell-side analysts are constructing the case that Canadian gold producers — from majors like Agnico Eagle to mid-tiers and select TSXV developers — are priced at price-to-net-asset-value multiples not seen since early 2021, despite operating margins at record highs on $4,600+ gold. The argument: when generalist investors rotate back into the sector, equities historically leverage gold's price by 2–3x on the upside, meaning the current discount may be the last opportunity to enter before that re-rating closes the gap.
